The event is hosted at the ultra high speed Spa Francorchamps circuit. A single mistake can cost you dearly on this track; keep your calm and pass your opponents carefully.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial Event using Rally Cars. Though any rally car is allowed, we recommend newer four wheel drives rather then older two wheel drives. Be careful not to speed too quickly into corners as they are tight and can cause you to hit the walls. It will be safer to reduce your speed before the corner, and then take it into a power drift with the throttle. You may find that some corners will give you more points if you stick to the inside of the turn. Test a variety of driving patterns to match the car you've selected.

You may find that some corners will give you more points if you stick to the inside of the turn. Test a variety of driving patterns to match the car you've selected.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial Event using non-racing versions of Mazda's lightweight front engine, rear wheel drive sportscar, the Roadster and MX-5. The Roadster/MX-5 doesn't have a lot of power starting off, so the first step to take when tuning is increasing power. An addition of a turbo is recommended as it is cost effective and gives you much more torque. On the track, be careful of losing control as there are steep ascents and descents. Section 2 and the last section will especially cause a large load shift up and down, and can lead into a sudden oversteer, so take head of this as you enter the corner.

description.JP: The way you handle the course will depend on the car. Lighter racing cars will need to be careful of hitting cornerstones too hard as it will upset their stability. Cornerstones especially on the inside of turn 2 can cause your car to oversteer as soon as you hit it with your tyre, and needs special care. On the other hand, if the car has a certain amount of weight, it will not be affected by cornerstones as much, and you will have more freedom in deciding your racing lines. If you wish to record stable laps, four wheel drives are relatively heavier and may prove to be a good choice.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial Event using European non-racing cars with 550PP or less. As long as it is 2 wheel drive the engine layout is not restricted. Though European cars are wide and varied, 2 wheel drives with a certain level of speed naturally tend to be mid engined cars. To mark a good time in a powerful mid engine rear wheel drive (MR), it is important to drive without sliding out the rear as much as possible. This is due to the common handling characteristic of an MR, in which a tail slide will greatly upset the stability of its angle while cornering. Operate the throttle carefully, and drive to maximise tyre grip. Because there are many turns in Ascari, it may also be effective to select closer ratio gears for the transmission.

The long flat out sections in the beginning and end are points for overtaking, use slip streams of other cars effectively to get ahead!

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event using racing cars. Though a wide selection of cars are available to choose from, you should probably select a touring based racing or rally car, rather than a single seater. And though high powered cars are easier to initiate into a drift, their control is also more difficult; try to select a car that fits your skill level. Of the four scoring sections, the one that will have the most effect on the total score, because of its difficulty, will be the second section at the 130R turn. It would be best to go full throttle into the corner and initiate the drift using only the steering operation, but since you'll be drifting at high speed, care must be taken to avoid applying too much countersteer.

It would be best to go full throttle into the corner and initiate the drift using only the steering operation, but since you'll be drifting at high speed, care must be taken to avoid applying too much countersteer.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event using American non-racing cars. This track requires high speed drifting, so it will be more advantageous to select cars with a long wheelbase that will be easier to stabilise in a drift. For tuning, American cars tend to have a lot of power to start with, so focus more on reducing weight and its suspension settings. Adjusting the suspension setup will greatly affect the outcome, especially at the section containing three repeating corners. Balance the tire grip and adjust the suspension to a hardness that is easier for you to control.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event for Rally Cars with 550PP or less. The hardest part about the Eiger Nordwand K Trail is not that it has both tarmac and dirt sections, it's the sheer lenght of the course. Driving the entire distance without touching the walls will be the biggest challenge, requiring you to be extremely careful when driving. Make sure to slow down well before the corners, as the course width is very narrow and even a small amount of extra speed will cause you to graze the walls. Start off by trying to run a safe clean lap, then slowly increase your speed with each successive lap.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using non-racing cars with 500PP or less. Setting fast lap times on the Mount Panorama Motor Racing Circuit depends on how fast you get through the technical section midway through the track. Though you need power for the long flat out sections at the beginning and end of the course, it will be easier to improve your lap time if you reduce weight and tune your suspension. On the other hand, if you are confident about your skill through the middle section, you could go for a power heavy setting. Set up your car according to its characteristics and your driving style.

description.JP: This is an expert level racing event in which you attempt to overtake as many rival cars as possible within 2 laps. Racing cars with 700PP or less are allowed in the race. The 13km long Circuit de la Sarthe, known as the stage of the Le Mans 24 Hour Race, has many straights where you can put your foot down. This makes the effective use of slip streams much more important. Rather than taking risks at the corners, it will be better to try and pass at the flat out sections.

description.JP: This is an intermediate level racing event in which you attempt to overtake as many rival cars as possible within 5 laps. Non-racing cars with 600PP or less are allowed in the race. The best overtaking points at the Nürburgring GP/F are at the entry from the home straight into the first corner, and the entry from the back straight into the Veedol chicane. Use slip streams and late braking to get ahead!

The stage is set at the famous Brands Hatch Indy Circuit, one of the founding pillars of motor racing in the UK. Make sure to raise your exit speed out of the first and last turns, to allow you to overtake in the flat out sections that follow!

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event on the Tokyo Route 246, using the 5th Vision Gran Turismo car, the NISSAN CONCEPT 2020 Vision Gran Turismo. You can acquire the NISSAN CONCEPT 2020 Vision Gran Turismo just by participating in this event*. Nissan has established a solid name for itself in Grand Touring over its 80 year history, with its cars finding the perfect balance between performance and comfort. Experience for yourself the next generation GT concept car of Nissan! *A full lap must be completed, regardless of whether the lap time is valid or not.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event using four wheel drive non-racing cars. Four wheel drives are known for their high stability, and setting the car to reduce that stability for drifting will be the key to performance. The adjustment of front to rear drive distribution will be a requirement, and the more drive force you apply to the rear, the easier it will become to drift. However stability will be lost at the same time, and you will need to find a good balance. While driving, how long you can maintain full throttle will be important. Set your car so that you can keep the car at full throttle once you enter a drift in any section.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event for non-racing versions of Ferrari's. Ferrari's are available in front engine and mid engine rear wheel drives, and though Mid engine cars will give you an advantage for higher scores, they are also harder to control. Using a front engine model instead is another option. The last section on this course is the place to really show your skill, and it would be best to drift from the 2nd turn after entering the scoring area, but you could also just focus on the approach to the final corner. If you clear the final corner with a large radius, you will naturally achieve a high score. Try not to drop your speed too much, and control the amount of slide by adjusting the throttle.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial Event using non-racing cars with 450PP or less. The Tsukuba circuit is a track in which a difference in power won't really affect the laptime as much. Though it depends on the car, if there is adequate power in its stock state, you will be better off reducing its weight up to the PP restriction. In addition you will of course need transmission and suspension tuning for better times, but reinforcing the drivetrain such as the clutch and drive shafts will also increase acceleration performance. Optimize your budget to find the best settings for the car.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the Fl car driven by Ayrton Senna. This car cannot be modified, so its settings are important in making it fast and easy to control. The settings for the downforce and gear ratios will be key here. In regards to downforce, the straight-line speed will become decreased the stronger it is set, however this will also greatly increase cornering speed which leads to better laptimes. Make adjustments while keeping an eye on the front to rear balance.

It will be necessary to be patient at times, to avoid risks in dangerous sections. Take extra special care in sections with repeating corners!

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event using the triplet siblings of the Toyota 86, Scion FR-S, and Subaru BRZ. Because the cars are slightly underpowered in their normal state, you'll need to first improve their power output. It will be effective to then adjust the suspension and drivetrain to match the power. The Madrid city course/reverse has many tricky mid-speed corners, and you'll need to mind your speed and set your lines properly to avoid hitting the walls. There are two spots where you need to cut back, and it will be important to maintain your drift without losing your balance here. Try to maintain your drift all the way to the exit of the last left hand turn.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event using only a Tuned car produced by a famous tuning shop. Most of these cars are high powered, so the focus will be on setting up the car so that its handling is more suited for drifting. Suspension and drivetrain are of course important, but if the car has too much power and is difficult to control, you could also use the power limiter to suppress the engine output. The Eiger Nordwand Short Track has many tight corners so be careful not to spin out. Especially in the first and second sections where you need to cut back in the tight turns, how you maintain your drift here will have a major effect on your score.

Suspension and drivetrain are of course important, but if the car has too much power and is difficult to control, you could also use the power limiter to suppress the engine output. The Eiger Nordwand Short Track has many tight corners so be careful not to spin out. Especially in the first and second sections where you need to cut back in the tight turns, how you maintain your drift here will have a major effect on your score.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using a GT500 racing car with 600PP or less. The Mazda Raceway Laguna Seca consists of mid- to low-speed corners. Quick lap times on this circuit will depend on gaining traction at corner exits as well as cornering speeds in the mid-speed turns. Though GT500 cars produce a lot of torque from their low RMP range, it can be an effective option to shorten the gears to improve traction, though this is not absolutely necessary. Of course increasing aerodynamic downforce will also improve your lap times. Last but not least, rather than braking at the last possible moment into the bends, it is recommended that your focus is placed more on the exits to the corners, to set yourself up for an earlier acceleration out of the turns.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using a non-racing car with 600PP or less. Although it is a mountainous course the Matterhorn Dristelen consists of mid- to high-speed corners, requiring a car with high power and stability. To quicken lap times, suspension settings will be important in addition to reducing weight. If you have difficulty stabilising the car at the flat out corners, remember that adding aerodynamic parts is an effective option.

description.JP: This is a beginners' level racing event in which you attempt to overtake as many rival cars as possible within 3 minutes, driving a non-racing car with 500PP or less. The event is hosted on the Twin Ring Motegi West Course. How you make the most of slip streams in the two straights will determine the outcome. The West shortcut in the last section is a place to brake as late as possible to get ahead!

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event using 2 wheel drive race cars. Mid engine rear wheel drives (MR) are recommended for higher scores, but MR's are harder to control, and you may find front engine rear wheel drives to be more manageable. In addition, touring car racers and rally cars are generally more suited for drifting in comparison to pure racing cars. If too much power is making it hard to handle, you could also consider de-tuning the car to lower its power. As for the course, Grand Valley has relatively tall cornerstones so you'll need to set lines that avoid riding over them too much. The scoring sections are relatively long and you'll also need to make sure you can maintain a long drift throughout section.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event using Japanese cars Produced in or before 1979. Older cars do not have a lot of power, so the first step is boosting the engine's output. In addition, many models sit fairly high with soft suspension, so you'll want to lower the ride height and set the suspension harder for better drift control. In regards to the track, the first and second sections should be considered as one section, and you'll want to drift continually through them. You'll tend to score higher if you set your entry speed a bit lower and set your driving line on the inside. For gaining lots of points, the third and final sections are key. Try to maintain your drift when you switch directions!

In addition, many models sit fairly high with soft suspension, so you'll want to lower the ride height and set the suspension harder for better drift control. In regards to the track, the first and second sections should be considered as one section, and you'll want to drift continually through them. You'll tend to score higher if you set your entry speed a bit lower and set your driving line on the inside. For gaining lots of points, the third and final sections are key. Try to maintain your drift when you switch directions!

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using non-racing cars with 500PP or less. Traction and turning is important on this track due to its many mid to low speed corners. Rather than selecting a large bodied car, it will be more advantageous to select a compact car with a shorter wheelbase. In regards to tuning, if it has enough power to begin with you'll want to raise PP by reducing the weight of the car. To aim for the Gold prize you'll definitely need to tune the drivetrain and transmission. Set the car so that it allows you to escape out of corners quickly and accelerate at full throttle.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the “Formula Gran Turismo“; Gran Turismo's original Formula car. This car cannot be modified or tuned so its settings are everything when matching the car to your driving style. In its initial configuration the car will tend to oversteer. If you dislike this initial characteristic, you could increase downforce in the rear, or even add more weight to the front to change the front to rear weight balance.

description.JP: This is an expert level race event in which you attempt to overtake as many cars as possible within 5 laps. Front engine, rear wheel drive (FR) non-racing cars with 500PP or less can participate in the event. FR's become trickier to control as their power increase, and they require sensitive throttle work. Slamming the accelerator pedal in a corner will just make your car spin out; you need to feel and predict the limits of your tyre grip while you open the throttle gradually. It's also effective to just set the TCS settings higher to do this for you.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event using any racing car. The majority of the scoring sections are mid- to high-speed corners, so you will be required to perform a series of high speed drifts. Harder suspension settings are recommended for this reason; however if you make the suspension too hard the handling of the car will start to become overly sensitive, so you will want to make adjustments while gradually feeling out the changes in drive feel. The place for gaining lots of points at Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps is through the 3rd and 4th sections. Through both sections you will have to make sure that your drift is not interrupted. The throttle should basically be to the floor for the most part, with partial throttle only used to reestablish control. You should make sure that the throttle is never lifted off completely.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event using German rear-wheel drive non-racing cars. If you're looking to score high, cars with good rear traction like mid-engine/rear-wheel drives (MR) and rear-engine/rear-wheel drives (RR) are recommended. However, they will be slightly harder to control compared to front-engine/rear-wheel drives (FR), so if you want more stability a (FR) may be a better choice. The Trial Mountain Circuit has a relatively wide track width, so using the full width of the course when driving is the secret to higher scores. The high-speed part of the first section will surely test your bravado; aim for a driving line that barely skims the wall!

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using four wheel drive non-racing cars with 550PP or less. The key to driving fast on this course lies in maintaining stability in its many lengthy mid- to high-speed corners. Set the car up to minimise understeer so that it will allow you to accelerate quickly out of the corners. In 4WD cars, it is effective to lessen the drive force of the front wheels, and supply more power to the rear wheels. In addition, the balance between the hardness of the suspension and the negative camber angle will greatly affect the amount of grip, so try a variety of settings to find the one that suits you best.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using Ayrton Senna's 1983 West Surrey Racing car with 551PP or less. Because this car cannot be tuned or modified, the shortcut to a gold prize rests in tweaking the settings to match the course and your driving preference. While this is an urban course with tight corners where higher downforce will help, the engine power is relatively low so overdoing it will slow you down. It also has a long flat-out section, so if you can cover the lack of downforce in corners with your driving skill alone, you may get a better time if you set the downforce lower. Balance your car between downforce and handling, and its gear ratio setup.

Balance your car between downforce and handling, and its gear ratio setup.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event on the Mount Panorama Motor Racing Circuit using the 7th Vision Gran Turismo, the Toyota FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo. You will receive a Toyota FT-1 Vision Gran Turismo just by participating in this event*. This is the Toyota FT-1 sports desing concept tuned and modified as a pure racing machine. Take this opportunity to grab its steering wheel, and enjoy its next-level driving performance! *You must complete a full lap, regardless of whether the lap time is valid or not.

description.JP: This is an intermediate level race event where you attempt to raise your position as much as you can by overtaking cars within a set number of laps. You can choose from non-race cars with 500PP or less. The London City course with its repetitive tight corners require settings focusing on acceleration rather than top speed. Cross your gear ratios and raise your speed quickly out of the turns to overtake your rivals.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event using any Lamborghini non-racing car. Lamborghini's are available in four-wheel drives (4WD) and mid-engine rear wheel drives (MR). For stability a 4WD is better, but if you want higher scores in drifting, you'll want to use an MR. These will be trickier to drive, but it will be much easier to keep the car drifting for a distance, such as in Section 2 of this track. If you're confident about your skill, definitely select an MR. The section for gaining the most points is also Section 2. There are 3 scored sections, so how well you fare here will greatly affect your score. In addition, because of the characteristics of this track, a mistake will generally mean you will hit the guard rails. Be careful of your driving line and entry speed!

These will be trickier to drive, but it will be much easier to keep the car drifting for a distance, such as in Section 2 of this track. If you're confident about your skill, definitely select an MR. The section for gaining the most points is also Section 2. There are 3 scored sections, so how well you fare here will greatly affect your score. In addition, because of the characteristics of this track, a mistake will generally mean you will hit the guard rails. Be careful of your driving line and entry speed!

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event using four-wheel drive (4WD) non-racing cars. Because 4WD cars are very stable, it is important to set the car to accommodate drifting. First and foremost you need to increase the amount of drive force to the rear tyres to achieve this. In addition, 4WD cars tend to be heavier, so you'll also want to increase engine power. If you want to save on PP for engine tuning, you could also install a 'Nitro Kit'. In regards to the track, you must be careful of going too fast into a corner with poor visibility – there are many blind corners due to the inclined track. In Section 2 there is also a jumping spot you'll need to watch for. The final section can gain you the most time, but again, make sure you don't overdo it into the turns.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using racing cars with 700PP or less. Racing cars reaching up to 700PP are extremely powerful and require careful control of the throttle, especially those with two-wheel drive. If you have issues driving a clean lap because of the excess power, you can increase the strenght of the TCS, or alternatively select a four-wheel drive car that is more stable to begin with. The course may appear to be more advantageous to cars with low downforce, but balance is key. Even if you are faster in the straights, if it slows you down that much more in the corners it will not be optimum. Set the downforce to match your driving style and type of car, and don't forget to adjust the gear ratios accordingly.

If you have issues driving a clean lap because of the excess power, you can increase the strenght of the TCS, or alternatively select a four-wheel drive car that is more stable to begin with. The course may appear to be more advantageous to cars with low downforce, but balance is key. Even if you are faster in the straights, if it slows you down that much more in the corners it will not be optimum. Set the downforce to match your driving style and type of car, and don't forget to adjust the gear ratios accordingly.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using a non-racing Lexus LFA car with 580PP or less. Japan's leading supercar, the Lexus LFA, is a bit tricky in terms of handling in its stock state. The objective of tuning will be to tune the car to suit your driving style. If you dislike the oversteer characteristic apparent in this car, adjust the weight balance by putting a heavier ballast in the front. Also the suspension is fairly soft to begin with, and hardening the damper alone will immediately sharpen the steering response. Solely adjusting the suspension settings will improve controllability considerably. Find the best setting simply by trial and error.

description.JP: This is an expert level race event where you attempt to overtake as many rival cars as possible within a set number of laps, on the Spa-Francorchamps in rainy weather. Non-racing cars with 500PP or less may participate in this event. The biggest challenge on this track is how you deal with the slippery surface and low visibility due to the rain. Even small mistakes in wet conditions can lead to a major loss of time; if you're not used to the track yet, first work on completing laps without making mistakes.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event using racing cars with 550PP or less. You can select from a wide variety of cars, but 4-wheel drive or rear-wheel drive racing cars and rally cars with a low ride height are recommended for this event. While there are 3 scoring sections, the first and second sections require a fairly long-distance drift; you'll want to set your gears shorter, and if you are using a rear-wheel drive you'll want to set the limited-slip differential stronger, so that you can easily force it into a power oversteer if necessary. In addition, it will be easy to spin out in both the first and second sections, due to the ups and downs of the track; work your throttle very carefully!

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial Event for Japanese non-racing cars. The narrow course width means that the recommended car here will be one that is relatively compact. The shorter the car's wheelbase is, the easier it will be to swing around quickly in combined corners. Because there are numerous small scoring sections, it will be important to have a grasp on how all of them work together in order to aim for a gold prize. Setting your racing lines to stay close to the record line will do the trick. The final section counts the most towards your score; if you feel that the banked curve is ending your drift prematurely, you can also use Nitrous to get your car to power drift!

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using race cars with 550PP or less. There are many ups and downs on this track, with mid- to low-speed corners. You'll want traction to accelerate quickly out of these. Considering this characteristic of the track, cars with 4-wheel drive (4WD) drivetrains will have an advantage over 2-wheel drive (2WD) cars. If you do decide to go with a 2WD, it is important to set the car so that it does not oversteer when you give it throttle. You'll need to place further focus on the drivetrain and alignment, setting the limited-slip differential (LSD) stronger and the rear toe further in. Regardless of the selected drivetrain type, the car will be prone to lift when going over crests, so adding some downforce will be another effective method of tuning for this track.

You'll want traction to accelerate quickly out of these. Considering this characteristic of the track, cars with 4-wheel drive (4WD) drivetrains will have an advantage over 2-wheel drive (2WD) cars. If you do decide to go with a 2WD, it is important to set the car so that it does not oversteer when you give it throttle. You'll need to place further focus on the drivetrain and alignment, setting the limited-slip differential (LSD) stronger and the rear toe further in. description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using a Nissan GT-R NISMO '14 with 600PP or less. Though it is up to the driver whether to use the available PP on engine power or weight reduction, we recommend making reducing weight a priority, as the car is rather heavy. Set the gears for a high-speed course, and adjust your suspension to be able to handle the tight infield. If you reduce its weight, you can set the suspension slightly softer to avoid going wide in the corners.

description.JP: This is an expert level race event where you attempt to overtake as many rival cars as possible within a set number of laps. Non-racing cars with 550PP or less can participate in the race. In this 1-lap race on the Nürburgring Nordschleife, you'll need to watch the movements of rival cars and pass each one carefully and smoothly. Your greatest enemy here will be making driving mistakes!

Non-racing cars with 550PP or less can participate in the race. In this 1-lap race on the Nürburgring Nordschleife, you'll need to watch the movements of rival cars and pass each one carefully and smoothly. Your greatest enemy here will be making driving mistakes!
